summary: Backend-only testing of dual payment-processor routing (Stripe for US, WiPay for Caribbean). Created /app/backend/tests/test_payment_options_routing.py with 11 tests — all PASS. Covered: 401/404 guards, TT merchant→wipay, US merchant→stripe (4 country-name variants), other Caribbean (Jamaica)→wipay, no-country fallback→wipay (reason='default'), plus regression of both WiPay and Stripe session-creation endpoints. Restaurants were seeded directly in Mongo with the required address.country and orders placed against them via POST /api/orders.
critical_code_review_comments: _vendor_country_for_order only reads restaurants/businesses/car_rental_companies — if future vendor collections are added (e.g. laundry, taxi), routing will silently default to WiPay. Consider centralising vendor lookup via _resolve_vendor_for_user.

payment-options endpoint returns processor='wipay' with reason='default' when merchant address has no country. This is intentional per spec, but frontend/CheckoutPage.js should surface a soft warning to ops when reason='default' so merchants missing country data can be fixed.
seed_data_creation: For each routing test the suite inserts a fresh restaurants doc with id prefix 'rest_qa_' and a chosen address.country, then places an order. Module-scoped autouse fixture purges all rest_qa_* docs at teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_payment_options_routing.py can be reused for regression. It seeds/deletes rest_qa_* restaurants and relies on conftest customer fixtures. Both WiPay (sandbox) and Stripe (test-mode) checkout session endpoints returned real hosted URLs.
rca of the issue: N/A — new feature working as specified.
